summary: A plain <tr>. Hover is CSS-only; a row is not itself interactive.
useWhen: every row, in either TableHead or TableBody

useInstead.when: the whole row should be clickable
useInstead.why: put the link or Button in a cell — nesting an interactive role on <tr> is not valid HTML

selection.note: renders a leading Checkbox cell — a <th scope="col"> select-all inside TableHead, a <td> inside TableBody. Takes the checkbox's own props rather than a boolean, since a selectable row needs `checked`/`onChange` wiring

guarantees: hover comes from CSS `:hover` plus a `data-hovered` escape hatch, not React Aria — a row takes no focus and fires no click, so there is no keyboard-versus-pointer distinction to track
the selection cell's element follows the section it sits in
requires: every row-selection Checkbox to be labelled — those boxes have no visible label by design, so see Checkbox's own contract
`isSelected` alongside a checked selection checkbox, so the row's state is not carried by colour alone
notes: TableRow itself is never named — a <tr> is not an interactive element and takes no accessible name. The naming requirement above belongs to the Checkbox inside it.

antiPatterns.why: it takes no focus, so a keyboard user can never fire it
a checkbox that cannot be changed reads as broken rather than as disabled
the row is tinted with nothing announcing why
